finding.claim: JSON body flattening joins object keys with '.' without escaping and writes every flattened key into one map with last-write-wins. A nested member {"a":{"b":X}} and a literal key "a.b" collide on json.a.b. A payload placed in the nested member is overwritten by a benign value under the dotted key and never reaches any rule-visible collection.
finding.source: HTTP request body with JSON content, when the JSON body processor is active (standard for JSON rule sets via ctl:requestBodyProcessor=JSON). Attacker sends {"a":{"b":"' OR 1=1--"},"a.b":"benign"}. No privilege needed.
finding.sink: ARGS_POST / ARGS entry json.a.b, which is what SQLi/XSS rules inspect. The backend application still receives the nested a.b value (standard JSON parsers keep it distinct from the literal key 'a.b').

trace.note: ProcessRequest calls readJSON(ss, RequestBodyRecursionLimit)
readJSON parses with gjson and calls readItems(json, "json", ...)
json.ForEach visits members in document order: first "a", then "a.b"
For key "a" (object) it recurses with objKey="json.a"
Nested key "b" is appended, giving objKey="json.a.b"
res["json.a.b"] = PAYLOAD
Top-level key "a.b" is appended, giving the same objKey="json.a.b" (no escaping of '.')
res["json.a.b"] = "benign" overwrites PAYLOAD; PAYLOAD is gone
Only the surviving map entries are copied into ArgsPost via col.SetIndex (lines 34-36)

finding.guards_checked: Only the recursion depth limit (default 1024, waf.go:33-34), which does not stop key collisions. gjson.Valid (line 90) passes for valid JSON. No duplicate-key or key-escaping check. Rules see only json.a.b = "benign".

finding.claim: The URLENCODED body processor is selected only on an exact string match of the lowercased Content-Type. A value with a parameter, such as 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8', never sets the processor. ProcessRequestBody then returns without parsing, so ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY are empty and form payloads are never inspected. The multipart branch uses HasPrefix and handles parameters; the URLENCODED branch does not, so the two are inconsistent.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled Content-Type request header on a POST with a form body, e.g. 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded; charset=UTF-8'. No privilege needed.
finding.sink: Body inspection (ARGS_POST, REQUEST_BODY) for SQLi/XSS/command rules. The origin framework still parses the form (standard frameworks ignore the charset parameter).

trace.note: AddRequestHeader switches on lowercased key 'content-type'
val := strings.ToLower(value), which keeps '; charset=utf-8'
Exact equality with "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" is false, so reqbodyProcessor is not set to URLENCODED
Multipart uses HasPrefix, so multipart with parameters IS handled (inconsistency)
ProcessRequestBody reads rbp = reqbodyProcessor, which is empty
rbp == "" (ForceRequestBodyVariable is false by default, line 210): Eval(PhaseRequestBody) runs with no body variables and returns at 1120
urlencoded ProcessRequest never runs, so ARGS_POST and REQUEST_BODY stay empty

finding.guards_checked: ForceRequestBodyVariable (default off); no fallback processor selection; no ctl:requestBodyProcessor in the library itself. Impact depends on the deployed rule set: if rules force URLENCODED for this content type, the bypass does not apply. The rule set is not in this tree, so this was not verified against CRS.

finding.claim: When url.ParseRequestURI rejects the request target, ProcessURI skips all query extraction. ExtractGetArguments (line 853) and the QUERY_STRING assignment (line 856) run only on success; the error branch (lines 836-839) sets path to the whole URI and query to empty, and the commented-out fallback (lines 841-851) was disabled. ARGS_GET, ARGS and QUERY_STRING are therefore empty for these requests.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled HTTP request target that Go's strict parser rejects, e.g. '/x%zz?id=1%27%20OR%201=1--' (a bad escape in the path makes ParseRequestURI fail), sent through a connector that passes the raw target to the framework.
finding.sink: ARGS_GET / ARGS / QUERY_STRING, which SQLi/XSS rules match. The origin application may still parse the query string from the raw target.

trace.note: ProcessURI(uri, ...) entry
url.ParseRequestURI(uri) returns an error for an invalid percent escape in the path
Error branch: urlencodedError set; path = uri (includes '?...')
Commented-out fallback that would extract arguments from the raw query is disabled
ExtractGetArguments runs only in the success branch, so it is skipped
queryString.Set(query) with query == ""

finding.guards_checked: No fallback extraction in the error branch. urlencodedError is set (line 837) and may trigger protocol rules in some rule sets. REQUEST_URI_RAW and REQUEST_LINE still carry the payload, so rules on those still match. Go's net/http server rejects such targets itself, so exploitation needs a connector that forwards raw targets to a more lenient origin. Medium confidence on exploitability; the code gap itself is clear.

finding.claim: ParseRequestReader uses bufio.Scanner with the default 64 KiB token limit and never checks scanner.Err(). A single header or body line longer than 64 KiB makes Scan return false silently. The header loop then ends early (line 479) and the body loop never runs (line 501), so the body is never written or inspected even though ProcessRequestBody still runs and returns no error.
finding.source: Raw HTTP request bytes given to the exported ParseRequestReader API. Attacker sends a header line or body line longer than 65536 bytes (e.g. a junk header or a single long body line) followed by a payload.
finding.sink: Request body inspection (REQUEST_BODY/ARGS_POST) and remaining headers (e.g. Content-Type, which decides body processing).

trace.note: bufio.NewScanner(data) with the default MaxScanTokenSize (64 KiB)
Scan() result ignored for the request line
Header loop: scanner.Scan() returns false on ErrTooLong, so the loop ends silently
ProcessRequestHeaders runs with truncated headers
Body loop: Scan() is false, so no body bytes are written
ProcessRequestBody runs on an empty buffer; scanner.Err() is never consulted

finding.guards_checked: No scanner.Err() check; no Buffer() enlargement. Caveat: the doc comment says 'DON'T USE IT FOR PRODUCTION yet', and in this tree the only callers are tests (transaction_test.go:123, 1843, 1904). Severity is limited to embedders who use this API on untrusted bytes. Verified by reading only; not executed.

finding.claim: FILES_SIZES is keyed by the client-supplied filename, and SetIndex(filename, 0, size) overwrites. Two file parts with the same filename leave only the last size recorded, so a per-file size rule can be evaded. FILES_COMBINED_SIZE (line 102) is still correct.
finding.source: Multipart/form-data request with two file parts that share a filename, e.g. first a large file then a tiny one, both named 'a.bin'. No privilege needed.
finding.sink: FILES_SIZES:<name> used by per-file upload size policies; the large file is still delivered to the application.

trace.note: filename := originFileName(p) from the attacker's Content-Disposition
filesCol.Add("", filename) appends both names
fileSizesCol.SetIndex(filename, 0, size) overwrites the first size with the second
FILES_COMBINED_SIZE still accumulates the true total

finding.guards_checked: FILES_COMBINED_SIZE is correct. Filename is never used as a filesystem path (only the CreateTemp pattern on line 64). Low impact: only per-file size rules are affected.
